clue.text: Frisky sort, one showing concern about physical exercise

indicators.note: about means going round, so the carer word wraps the exercise abbreviation

parts.note: someone who shows concern for others is a carer
PE is the usual abbreviation for physical education or exercise at school

explanation.surface: A lively person who worries about getting enough exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who capers leaps about playfully, so a frisky sort is one who cavorts.

clue.text: Rock concert's starting with Scott Joplin piece

indicators.note: starting means just the opening letter of concert is used

parts.note: Scott Joplin composed ragtime pieces such as The Entertainer, called rags

explanation.surface: A rock concert opens with a ragtime number.
explanation.definitionFit: A crag is a steep rugged mass of rock.

clue.text: Show insect's under leaf

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the insect after the leaf word

parts.note: a leaf of a book is a page
an ant is an insect; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: An exhibition where an insect hides beneath a leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a public show or spectacle, often a procession.

clue.text: Announced floral: tribute for broadcasting pioneer

indicators.note: announced means spoken out loud, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a wreath is a ring of flowers laid as a tribute

explanation.surface: A funeral tribute of flowers announced for a broadcasting pioneer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Reith was the first director-general of the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: John Reith founded and shaped the BBC as its first director-general.

clue.text: Preparation for exam in religious education faculty

parts.note: RE is the school abbreviation for religious education
sight or vision is one of the faculties, or senses

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a test in a university's religious studies department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faculty' suggests a university department, but it is a sense such as sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Revision is the British term for going back over material to prepare for an exam.

clue.text: With gusto, halved cheese roll

parts.note: brio is liveliness or gusto, as in playing with brio

indicators.note: halved means only the first half of the word cheese is kept

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly tucks into a cheese roll cut in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A brioche is a sweet French bread roll made with eggs and butter.

clue.text: Heard lover with ring portending what's to come?

indicators.note: heard means spoken out loud, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend or lover
ding is the sound of a bell ringing

explanation.surface: The sound of a lover's ring as a sign of things ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Boding is foretelling, giving an omen of what is to happen.

clue.text: See possibly drunken Peruvian faint across front of bar

parts.note: the Inca were the native people of ancient Peru

indicators.note: across means lying over, so the pale word straddles the letter from bar

parts.note: faint, as of a colour, means pale

indicators.note: front of means the opening letter of bar is used

explanation.surface: Look at a Peruvian who may be drunk going pale in front of the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link pointing to the clue that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Drunk and incapable is a British legal phrase for someone too intoxicated to look after themselves.

clue.text: "Cream with cold centre" would only partly describe this treat

definitions.text: "Cream with cold centre" would only partly describe this treat

parts.words: "Cream with cold centre" would only partly describe this treat
parts.note: a chocolate-coated ice-cream bar: the cold cream is only the middle, and the description leaves out the chocolate outside

explanation.definitionFit: A choc ice is a block of ice cream coated in chocolate, sold as a treat.

clue.text: Display attitude, that's no longer current?

parts.note: ex is used for something former, as in ex-wife
a position or attitude is a stance on a matter

explanation.surface: Showing off a stance that has gone out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposition is a large public exhibition or display.

clue.text: Hurt resulting from dagger I've wielded

indicators.note: a weapon that is wielded is swung about, so the letters of dagger and I've are moved around

explanation.surface: A wound inflicted by a dagger someone has brandished.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling hurt and feeling aggrieved both describe resentment at being wronged.

clue.text: Chew mark in piece of meat

indicators.note: in places the mark abbreviation inside the cut of meat

parts.note: a chop is a cut of meat such as lamb or pork
M is short for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A bite mark left in a chop.
explanation.definitionFit: To chomp is to chew noisily and vigorously.

clue.text: Contorted in a Spanish dance, suffer these?

definitions.text: Contorted in a Spanish dance, suffer these?

indicators.note: contorted means twisted out of shape, so the letters of the phrase are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A dancer bent into odd shapes in a flamenco will pay for it afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the letters of A SPANISH DANCE rearrange to the answer, and the clue as a whole describes what a contorted dancer suffers.
explanation.definitionFit: Aches and pains are the minor bodily discomforts that follow strenuous or awkward exertion.

clue.text: Often changing precise time prisoner is to be admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the prisoner goes inside the moment word

parts.note: an instant is an exact moment in time
con is short for convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: A prison keeps changing the exact time an inmate is let in.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconstant means fickle, given to frequent change.

clue.text: Symbolic set of books kept by community

indicators.note: kept by means held inside, so the books abbreviation sits within the community word

parts.note: a nation is a community of people sharing a country
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A community preserves a collection of books.
explanation.definitionFit: A notation is a system of symbols, as in musical or mathematical notation.

clue.text: One's on track to be a current supplier

definitions.text: One's on track to be a current supplier

parts.words: One's on track to be a current supplier
parts.note: the reading is not a hopeful candidate but a rail beside the railway track that supplies electric current to trains

explanation.definitionFit: A third rail runs alongside the tracks and carries electricity to power trains.

clue.text: Aim to express disapproval?

definitions.meaning: an aim or goal is the ... of an action

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means a purpose and the verb means to protest, two senses of one spelling.

clue.text: One is released from decaying missile

indicators.note: released from means let go, so the letter for one is removed

parts.note: perishing means rotting or decaying
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something is freed from a rotting missile.
explanation.definitionFit: Pershing was a US ballistic missile named after General John Pershing.

clue.text: Plant displayed in porch, ideally

indicators.note: displayed in means the letters are on show inside the words porch, ideally

explanation.surface: A plant would ideally be shown off in a porch.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is a flowering plant with showy, often exotic blooms.

clue.text: Half of case is filled with unwieldy steel instrument

indicators.note: filled with means the half word is stuffed with the rearranged letters
half of means only the first two letters of case are used
unwieldy means awkward to handle, so the letters of steel are moved about

explanation.surface: Half a case is packed with an awkward steel musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of case' looks like a fraction of a container, but it is just the opening two letters; 'unwieldy' is the anagram signal, not a description of the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A celesta is a keyboard instrument whose hammers strike steel plates.

clue.text: So-called massacre — safe to look. round?

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
lo is an old word meaning look or behold
a round shape like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a so-called massacre is a safe thing to go round and look at.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1819 Manchester killings are called a massacre ironically, with a name modelled on Waterloo; 'peter' as a safe is thieves' slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Peterloo was the 1819 attack on a reform meeting in Manchester, mockingly nicknamed after Waterloo.

clue.text: Messenger, ultimately the beneficiary of a will

parts.note: a legate is an envoy or messenger, especially of the Pope

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of the word the is used

explanation.surface: In the end the messenger inherits under the will.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is a person who receives a legacy under a will.

clue.text: Pope, for example: western religious leader holding ceremony

indicators.note: holding means the two outer letters clasp the ceremony word between them
leader means the first letter of religious is taken

parts.note: a rite is a religious ceremony

explanation.surface: The Pope as a Western church leader presiding over a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope' looks like the head of the church, but it is the poet Alexander Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope was an eighteenth-century English poet and so an author.

clue.text: Girl giving directions for delivery leaves having taken this coat?

parts.note: Sal is a short form of the girl's name Sally
writing where a letter should go is addressing it

explanation.surface: A girl writes the address on parcels as she goes out wearing a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb about the girl departing, but it is the lettuce leaves, which a salad dressing coats.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad dressing is poured over lettuce leaves, coating them.

clue.text: Model given current treatment

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics
a deal is the way one is treated, as in a raw deal

explanation.surface: A model is getting the latest treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect example or model to follow.

clue.text: Smile, taking day, off from hard work

indicators.note: off from means removed from, so the day abbreviation comes out of the toil word

parts.note: a grind is tedious hard work

explanation.surface: Smiling at taking a day off from work.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a broad beaming smile that shows the teeth is a grin.

clue.text: Son tucked into a meal — not reached the port yet?

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside, so the son abbreviation goes within the meal phrase

parts.note: tea is a light afternoon or evening meal in Britain

explanation.surface: A boy eats his meal before the after-dinner port has come round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests the after-dinner drink, but a ship still at sea has not reached harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that has not yet reached port is still out on the ocean.

clue.text: Marks in essays teacher rejects each term

annotationWithheld.why: Marks in essays teacher rejects each term (9): TRIMESTER; 'term' defines it and M in TRIES gives TRIMES, but no reading of 'teacher rejects each' supplies the final TER, so a word is probably misread and there is no scan
annotationWithheld.clue: Marks in essays teacher rejects each term

clue.text: One comes before the big film, and one comes after

definitions.text: One comes before the big film
definitions.meaning: a preview of a coming film shown before the main feature in a cinema
something towed behind a vehicle, following it

explanation.definitionFit: A cinema preview is a trailer, and so is a wheeled cart towed behind a car.

clue.text: Coward, perhaps, and convict taken round ship

indicators.note: taken round means turned about, so both pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: Noel Coward was the playwright, so Noel is an example of a Coward
lag is slang for a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: A coward and a criminal are taken around on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' looks like a timid person, but it is the playwright Noel Coward; the whole of NOELLAG is turned to read GALLEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large sailing ship used especially by Spain in past centuries.
